primary_paper.title: Sleep drives metabolite clearance from the adult brain
key_metrics: Interstitial space volume fraction increases by ~60% (from ~14% awake to ~23% in natural slow-wave sleep).
Radiolabeled beta-amyloid clears roughly twice as fast during sleep compared with wakefulness.
Adrenergic receptor blockade in awake brains partially mimics the sleep-induced fluid influx.

supporting_papers.title: Psychophysiological insomnia: the behavioural model and a neurocognitive perspective
key_metrics: Repeatedly lying awake worrying pairs the mattress and pillow with threat vigilance via classical Pavlovian conditioning.
EEG around sleep onset shows elevated 14–35 Hz beta/gamma cortical fast activity despite bodily exhaustion.
Stimulus control therapy (leaving the bed after ~15–20 minutes awake) extinguishes bedroom conditioned arousal.

supporting_papers.title: The human emotional brain without sleep — a prefrontal amygdala disconnect
key_metrics: 26 healthy young adults randomized to normal sleep vs 35 hours of total sleep deprivation before fMRI emotional viewing.
Sleep-deprived amygdala shows a +60% surge in reactivity to aversive emotional scenes.
Functional connectivity between the medial prefrontal brake and the amygdala drops sharply while locus coeruleus coupling rises.

supporting_papers.title: Coupled electrophysiological, hemodynamic, and cerebrospinal fluid oscillations in human sleep
key_metrics: 13 healthy human sleepers scanned inside simultaneous EEG-fMRI during non-REM sleep.
Slow delta electrical waves (~0.05 Hz, roughly every 20 seconds) precede a drop in cortical blood volume.
As blood volume recedes, large macroscopic waves of cerebrospinal fluid surge upward through the fourth ventricle.

supporting_papers.title: Norepinephrine-mediated slow vasomotion drives glymphatic clearance during sleep
key_metrics: During natural NREM sleep, locus coeruleus norepinephrine rises and falls rhythmically every ~50 seconds, squeezing and relaxing pial arteries like a mechanical pump.
Common GABAergic sedative zolpidem (Ambien) induces sleep faster but flattens norepinephrine waves by ~50% and cuts glymphatic tracer inflow by ~30%+
